gloss: dramatic pose (in kabuki); striking a pose

definitions.gloss: dramatic pose (in kabuki); striking a pose
definitions.explanation: A stylized, frozen pose held by a kabuki actor at a climactic moment, often with crossed eyes and an exaggerated expression. By extension, any showy or boastful display of resolve.

examples.japanese: ⟦{役者|やくしゃ}→役者：05113_yakusha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{見得|みえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}った→切る：02693_kiru⟧。
examples.english: The actor struck a dramatic pose.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歌舞伎|かぶき}→歌舞伎：04455_kabuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{見得|みえ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{観客|かんきゃく}→観客：02556_kankyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一番|いちばん}→一番：01140_ichiban⟧⟦{盛|も}り{上|あ}がる→盛り上がる：06344_moriagaru⟧⟦{瞬間|しゅんかん}→瞬間：03226_shunkan⟧だ。
examples.english: The mie pose is the moment in kabuki when the audience gets most excited.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{絶対|ぜったい}→絶対：00435_zettai⟧⟦{勝|か}って→勝つ：01199_katsu⟧みせる」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧{見得|みえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}った→切る：02693_kiru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{惨敗|ざんぱい}→惨敗：08236_zanpai⟧だった。
examples.english: He made a big show of declaring "I'll definitely win," but the result was a crushing defeat.

notes:
Almost always appears in the idiom {見得|みえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ (to strike a dramatic pose). In the figurative sense, it describes making a bold declaration or showy display of resolve — often with an implication that the speaker may not deliver.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見得|みえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧: to strike a pose; to make a bold declaration
- ⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧{見得|みえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧: to make a grand show of resolve
- {見得|みえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}る→張る：12583_haru⟧: to put on airs (less common variant)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{見栄|みえ}→見栄：06626_mie⟧: vanity, showing off — same reading, related etymologically, but refers to outward appearance for social effect rather than a theatrical pose. ⟦{見栄|みえ}を{張|は}る→見栄を張る：15322_miewoharu⟧ = to keep up appearances
- ⟦ポーズ→ポーズ：11268_poozu⟧: pose — loanword, generic and modern
- {大言壮語|たいげんそうご}: big talk, grandiose words — emphasizes the boastful claim rather than the pose

prominent_see_also.note: vanity, showing off - same reading, different kanji
